meta.change: Chronology audit (cedwyn-documentary#14): every scene carries date_sort and is checked for order by tools/script_patch.py; 13 scenes moved to where they happened in the order, 31 re-dated from the Court of Appeal judgment or the site's published chronology, three scenes that showed Mary after her death in March 1983 corrected, the autumn 1974 sequence rewritten from the judgment, Billy's death shown once (the probate entry moves to the July 1991 grant), and act numbers made continuous. No scene dropped, no id changed, doors 1-44 keep their numbers, no video touched. Welsh and Spanish for the rewritten lines are machine-assisted, for native review. — Claude agent

why.F003A: Scene pack for door 5 written (scripts/F003A.json); not rendered.
why.F019A: The first signals crossed from Flat Holm to Lavernock on 13 May 1897, two days before the Evening Express scenes of 15 May; 'July 1897' was the date of a later report, not of the crossing.
why.F022A: John Williams the elder died on 17 July 1908 and was buried on 21 July (F023); his son can only take on both holdings after that.
why.F023B: The scene's own line gives his birth as about 1908-09; it was dated 1910.
why.F025C: Drain agreement dated 15 May 1924 on the register of WA735527.
why.F030A: The scene is the passing of the Act (Royal Assent 25 May 1939), not its pleading in 1974; the Act's start on 1 July 1940 is F032.
why.F036: The papers are taken (F036A, 1951) before Mary finds the box empty; the range c. 1950-52 allows it.
why.F037A: Court of Appeal: the last payment, at some time in 1953, was made under a judgment for arrears.
why.F037C: Court of Appeal: the tenancy, ended by notice to quit, expired on 2 February 1955.
why.F047A: Conveyance dated 11 June 1965 (released by the Vale of Glamorgan Council, 14 Sep 2026).
why.F047B: The family's date for the death is 1967 (Mary's account); the Court of Appeal gives 'at some time in the period 1965-67'. A death in 1966 and a burial in 1967 cannot both stand.
why.F051A: RCAHMW survey notes are dated 26 April 1974, eleven days after the open day of 15 April.
why.F053A: Court of Appeal: Judge Watkin Powell gave leave on 19 September 1974, the warrant not to be enforced until 31 October.
why.F053B: Court of Appeal: on 31 October 1974 the Trust wrote that it had withdrawn its instructions to the bailiff; the warrant itself was withdrawn in writing later, before 25 November.
why.F054: Court of Appeal: both letters were addressed to Mrs Buckler but sent to her solicitor, who received them on the morning of 4 November 1974; the judge then stayed execution. The Trust's letter reported a buyer; it was not an offer of sale to her.
why.F059A: A notice arriving after Mary's death cannot precede 26 March 1983.
why.F069: Mary died in March 1983; she cannot read the 1987 judgment.
why.F075: Mary died in March 1983; 'his mother' cannot be at the table in May 1988.
why.F082: Mary died in March 1983; 'his mother' cannot be in the lane in December 1988.
why.F071: A letter to the Minister on spot-listing follows the listing inspection of 29 July 1988; it cannot sit before the January 1988 petition. Day not recorded.
why.F071B: The news report covers the eviction (30 November) and the injunction (2-3 December); it cannot sit before January 1988. Broadcast day not recorded.
why.F082A: A court hearing is not held just after 4 a.m.; it is later the same day.
why.F085: 'Mid-December, before 21 December' follows the scene of about 12 December.
why.F086A: Published chronology: summons withdrawn in January 1989.
why.F093B: The probate calendar entry is made at the grant of July 1991; as a scene in April 1990 it had Billy dying a month before he died.
why.F093C: The Echo of Saturday 2 June 1990 reports that he died suddenly that week.
why.F103A: Transfer dated 10 November 1994 on the register of WA735527.
why.F106E: SI 2004/3391 came into force on 1 January 2005, not in 2004.
why.F115: The wiki went public on 22 September 2026; it was sitting before February 2026.
why.F126A: The county court's reply is dated 4 August 2026, not 13 August.
why.F130A: The four requests to the Royal Commission are dated 8 September 2026 (RC26-0375).

F019A.logline: Marconi's wireless signals cross the water from Flat Holm to Lavernock Point, a few miles from Llandough.

F019B.title: Ty-mawr on the map
F019B.logline: The 1900 map of Llandough names 'Ty-mawr' (Great House) beside St Dochdwy's Church.

F022A.logline: With his father buried, the younger John Williams takes on both holdings.

F028A.title: The eldest son is born
F028A.logline: Mary and Frederick's first son is born.

F030A.title: The Limitation Act is passed
F030A.logline: Parliament passes the Limitation Act 1939: after twelve years, an owner out of possession can no longer sue to recover land. It will come into force on 1 July 1940.

F037A.logline: Frederick makes what proves to be the last payment of rent, paid under a court judgment for arrears.

F037C.logline: The notice to quit runs out and Frederick Buckler's yearly tenancy ends.

F046A.title: A rumoured sale
F046A.logline: By a cousin's later account, the eldest son sells something through a solicitor, perhaps a parcel of the land, without his parents knowing. No document of it has been found.

F047B.date: 1967 (Mary's account; 1965–67 in the Court of Appeal judgment)

F048B.title: The eldest son's household leaves
F048B.logline: The eldest son and his household leave the farm.

F053A.logline: Judge Watkin Powell gives BP Pension Trust leave to enforce the 1962 possession order; the warrant is not to be enforced before 31 October. Mrs Buckler's solicitors prepare an appeal.

F053B.title: The bailiff is called off
F053B.logline: BP Pension Trust withdraws its instructions to the bailiff. Two letters to Mrs Buckler are written, one from the Trust and one from BP Properties, and sent to her solicitor.

F054.logline: On the morning of the hearing Mrs Buckler's solicitor receives the two letters dated 31 October. BP Pension Trust writes that it has found a buyer, BP Properties, and called off the bailiff; BP Properties offers her the house and garden rent-free for as long as she wishes. The judge stays execution. Mary neither accepts nor refuses.

F071.date: 1988 (after the inspection of 29 July; day not recorded)

F093B.title: Letters of administration
F093B.logline: Administration of Billy's estate is granted. The probate calendar enters his death as April 1990; the Echo of 2 June 1990 reported that he died that week.

F093C.logline: William “Billy” Buckler dies suddenly; he had long made a detour around Llandough so as never to pass the site of Great House Farm.

F106A.logline: The Freedom of Information Act receives Royal Assent.

F106E.logline: The Environmental Information Regulations come into force, on the same day as the right of access under the Freedom of Information Act.

F108A.title: The case in the lecture hall
F108A.logline: A land-law course's mind-map on adverse possession cites BP Properties v Buckler.

cy.logline: Mae'r Barnwr Watkin Powell yn rhoi caniatâd i BP Pension Trust orfodi gorchymyn meddiant 1962; ni chaiff y warant ei gweithredu cyn 31 Hydref. Mae cyfreithwyr Mrs Buckler yn paratoi apêl. (cyfieithiad peiriant)

es.logline: El juez Watkin Powell autoriza a BP Pension Trust a ejecutar la orden de posesión de 1962; la orden no podrá ejecutarse antes del 31 de octubre. Los abogados de la señora Buckler preparan una apelación. (traducción automática)

cy.logline: Mae BP Pension Trust yn tynnu ei gyfarwyddiadau i'r beili yn ôl. Ysgrifennir dau lythyr at Mrs Buckler, un gan y Trust ac un gan BP Properties, a'u hanfon at ei chyfreithiwr. (cyfieithiad peiriant)

es.title: Se retira al alguacil
es.logline: BP Pension Trust retira sus instrucciones al alguacil. Se escriben dos cartas a la señora Buckler, una del Trust y otra de BP Properties, y se envían a su abogado. (traducción automática)

cy.logline: Ar fore'r gwrandawiad daw'r ddau lythyr dyddiedig 31 Hydref i law cyfreithiwr Mrs Buckler. Mae BP Pension Trust yn ysgrifennu ei fod wedi cael prynwr, BP Properties, ac wedi galw'r beili yn ôl; mae BP Properties yn cynnig y tŷ a'r ardd iddi yn ddi-rent cyhyd ag y myn. Mae'r barnwr yn atal y gweithredu. Nid yw Mary yn derbyn nac yn gwrthod. (cyfieithiad peiriant)

es.logline: La mañana de la audiencia, el abogado de la señora Buckler recibe las dos cartas fechadas el 31 de octubre. BP Pension Trust escribe que encontró comprador, BP Properties, y que retiró al alguacil; BP Properties le ofrece la casa y el jardín sin alquiler por el tiempo que quiera. El juez suspende la ejecución. Mary no acepta ni rechaza. (traducción automática)

cy.logline: Rhoddir gweinyddiaeth ystad Billy. Mae'r calendr profiant yn cofnodi ei farw yn Ebrill 1990; adroddodd yr Echo ar 2 Mehefin 1990 iddo farw yr wythnos honno. (cyfieithiad peiriant)

es.title: Cartas de administración
es.logline: Se concede la administración de la sucesión de Billy. El calendario de sucesiones anota su muerte en abril de 1990; el Echo del 2 de junio de 1990 informó que murió esa semana. (traducción automática)
